maria.l: Anyone hit a weird bug with async client + tool/function calling where structured outputs get parsed twice or the tool gets invoked twice? :thinking_face:

jason: Yep, ran into that this morning. Repro steps below. I think it only shows up for async when using TypedDict returns.

jason: repro snippet:
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
from typing import TypedDict

class Resp(TypedDict):
    action: str
    value: int

client = AsyncClient(api_key=..., retry_policy=None)

async def call():
    res = await client.generate(
        model="open-lite-1",
        prompt="call tool to return JSON",
        tool_call={"name": "compute", "args_schema": Resp},
    )
    print(res.output)  # sometimes prints the object twice or prints the tool output AND the fallback text
```

alex: I saw a log where the runtime returned 502 for the toolcall and the SDK retried the whole request, which caused the tool to be executed twice (our tool is a webhook). Might be a retry+parse race.

shreya: can you paste the full raw response you get from the server? Also which SDK version?

jason: SDK 0.8.3. raw payload (redacted):
```json
{
  "id": "gen_123",
  "choices": [
    {
      "type": "tool_call",
      "tool": "compute",
      "tool_output": "{\"action\": \"increment\", \"value\": 7}",
      "structured": {"action": "increment", "value": 7}
    }
  ],
  "status": 200
}
```

maria.l: interesting — sometimes the SDK sees both `tool_output` string and `structured` object and tries to coerce both into a typed result, emitting two messages. In async path the parse flow awaits the tool executor future and there's a window where both parsers run.

shreya: can you try setting `client._config.retry_policy = "no_retry"` as a quick check? (I know internal fields, but just to confirm)

jason: did that, still saw duplicate messages but less frequent. When the webhook returned 500 the SDK retried and then the parsing step re-ran, causing duplicate structured parses that ended up in the final output list.

alex: this smells like a concurrency bug: parseOrderedResults() is not idempotent when awaited multiple times. We should make parsing atomic or attach a parsed flag to the choice item.

shreya: filing an issue + small reproduction test would help. I'll open a PR to add an integration test for async tool_call that stubs the tool webhook and returns 500 then 200.

maria.l: workaround for now: use the sync client or set `tool_call_parse=False` and run your own deterministic parsing (ugh). Also avoid webhook side-effects until we patch.

jason: workaround noted. Also seeing typing issues: the SDK's typehint for `tool_call.args_schema` expects a `Type[TypedDict] | dataclass | pydantic.BaseModel`, but mypy complains on union. Any plan to tighten the typing?

shreya: yes, follow-up request: make the typing more ergonomic — maybe overloads for `tool_call` param in stubs so autocompletion works better for TypedDicts. Added to the DX backlog.

ci-bot: CI: test/async-toolcall (integration) — failed on linux-py3.11 — see https://ci.redwood.example/runs/5467 :x:

alex: thanks CI — that failure matches the dup-call repro. I'm going to add a mutex around parsing in the async path and push a candidate fix.

shreya: if you can get a small patch + unit test, we'll ship a patch release. Please also include a changelog entry and a note in the release that async tool_call had duplicate-execution edge case.

alex: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3342 — simple guard + test. Also added a note about `RetryPolicy` interactions.

jason: tested PR branch, looks good locally. No double calls and typed parsing now returns a single TypedDict as expected. Thanks! :thumbsup:

maria.l: awesome — will hold off the webhook deploy until next release. Thanks for quick turnaround.

shreya: follow-up tasks: 1) improve type stubs for `tool_call`, 2) document `tool_call_parse` opt-out, 3) add example showing dataclasses + TypedDicts in async sample app.

maria.l: sounds good. Closing loop for now. If you hit regressions ping me. :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:
